newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai inflation news fails to lift gloomy investors.
newsitem.headline: Thai inflation news fails to lift gloomy investors.

text.p: Thai inflation rose only marginally in June, data released on Tuesday showed, but investors brushed the figures aside to focus on troubles in the finance sector and concerns over the local currency.
The consumer price index rose 4.4 percent year-on-year in June, largely in line with market expectations and against 4.3 percent in each of the previous two months, the Commerce Ministry said.

The ministry said a 20 percent rise in retail soft-drink prices in June contributed to a 5.7 percent year-on-year increase in food and beverage prices while the non-food category increased 3.4 percent.
On a month-on-month basis, the index rose a moderately low 0.2 percent in June.
Analysts said the relatively flat June CPI figure would have virtually no impact on Thailand's battered stock and financial markets when they reopened on Wednesday after a holiday.
Investors were more concerned with problems faced by local financial institutions and jitters over the stability of the baht which came under speculative attack in May.
"I don't think it could substantially cheer up the market even if the June figure was a flat zero. It has become a non-issue now," said an analyst at Multi-Credit Corp of Thailand Plc.
The central Bank of Thailand has since Friday suspended the business of 16 ailing finance companies for 30 days and given them two weeks to propose merger plans or be forced to consolidate.
The cash-strapped firms could not raise capital to offset sharp declines of their asset value this year, the central bank said.

Analysts said the market also focused on the prospects of Thailand's steady capital outflow in coming months after the central bank announced last week that the country posted a big monthly balance of payments deficit of 112.3 billion baht ($4.5 billion).
Thai foreign reserves fell $4 billion in May to a two-year low of $33.3 billion after the central bank was forced to intervene in local and foreign currency markets to defend the baht in mid-May.
"The main focus now is how to prevent the fallout of expected sustained capital outflow and problems of finance companies from spreading to the commercial bank sector," the Multi-Credit analyst said.

Another analyst at Dhana Siam Finance and Securities Plc said inflation for the whole of 1997 should ease to 4.2 percent against 4.5 percent projected by the central bank for this year and 5.9 last year.
Most analysts expected the Thai economy to expand at a decade low of less than five percent this year against 5.7 percent projected by the government and 6.4 percent in 1996.
